name: Hypophosphatemic Rickets

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and biochemical diagnostic criteria for hypophosphatemic rickets

criteria.description: Persistent hypophosphatemia due to renal phosphate wasting
Elevated or inappropriately normal serum fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) levels
Radiographic evidence of rickets including metaphyseal cupping and fraying
Positive family history consistent with X-linked dominant inheritance
Normal serum calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels despite rickets

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent hypophosphatemia with renal phosphate wasting, radiographic evidence of rickets, and elevated or inappropriately normal FGF23 levels
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for PHEX mutations can confirm diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypophosphatemia due to renal phosphate wasting
Metaphyseal cupping and fraying on radiographs
searchTerms: flared and irregular bone ends on x-ray
cupped and frayed growth plate appearance

common.symptomName: Bone pain localized to long bones
searchTerms: bone tenderness in arms or legs

common.symptomName: Dental abscesses due to defective dentin mineralization
searchTerms: dental abscesses due to poor tooth mineralization
tooth root infections from defective dentin

occasional.symptomName: Enthesopathy with calcification of tendons and ligaments
searchTerms: hardening where tendons connect to bone

occasional.symptomName: Hearing loss due to ossicular abnormalities
searchTerms: hearing loss from middle ear bone problems
impaired hearing from ear bone defects

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic bone disease
searchTerms: low energy due to bone illness
calcium buildup in kidneys after treatment

laboratory: Low serum phosphate due to renal phosphate wasting
Normal serum calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels
Elevated or inappropriately normal serum FGF23
imaging: Metaphyseal cupping, fraying, and widening on long bone X-rays
Bone deformities such as bowing of legs
Possible ossicular abnormalities on temporal bone imaging
genetic: Mutations in the PHEX gene (most common)
Other gene mutations: FGF23, DMP1, ENPP1
other: Positive family history consistent with X-linked dominant inheritance
Dental abnormalities including abscesses and hypoplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated FGF23 but no family history

redFlags: Severe bone deformities causing functional impairment
Development of nephrocalcinosis or renal impairment
references: Carpenter TO. The expanding family of hypophosphatemic syndromes. J Bone Miner Metab. 2012;30(1):1-9.
Imel EA, Econs MJ. Approach to the hypophosphatemic patient. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2012;97(3):696-706.
